shots.shows: The agent's terminal: system add syncs robnet's packages/ui (72 components, 73 stories, with warnings for stories that read no colour token and the kit's own off-scale values); session new --system; a commit refused for a raw <button> with className, an inline style, and literal padding and radius in the proposed component's CSS, each naming the kit token to write instead so theme tweaks reach it; then the clean commit; last, a freeform session (no --system) refuses a proposed/ folder with invalid_proposed
The Design systems page: robnet's UI library as a card with its version, component and story counts, and Sync; the add-a-library field above
A design system's Components tab: the searchable catalog down the left, every story rendered live from the synced kit in the gallery, the theme axes (data-theme, data-accent) above it
The gallery narrowed to one component, Card, rendering its story from the library

The catalog filtered by 'st': names that start with it first, so Stack, the layout primitive Brainstorm generated because the library has none and marked as Brainstorm's, leads; the gallery narrows to the matches' stories
The Theme tab: the library's theme axes and its tokens with their values per axis
The Warnings tab: what the sync noticed but didn't refuse: stories with no colour token, components with no story, values the kit itself writes off its scales

The meal-plan brainstorm as it opens: the first block, built only from robnet's Card, Item, Badge, Progress and Button, on the stage; the Inspector's controls and, below them, the Design system section

All slots on the board, each showing its picked variant: the week slot on its 'strip' variant (the sidebar lists its 'list' variant too) and the recipe card, all composed from the kit; the WeekStrip the kit lacked carries a 'not in system' tag
Close-up of the week-strip block: the proposed WeekStrip outlined with its 'WeekStrip · not in system' tag, beside kit components
The Inspector's Design system section: robnet's UI at v1, the theme axes, colour and size tokens, Save as theme, Export theme and Reset, and the proposed WeekStrip with Promote
The same brainstorm after three theme tweaks (dark, rose accent, 1rem radius): every block on the canvas follows, since they all read the kit's tokens, and the Inspector counts the tweaks
Saving the tweaks as a named theme of the design system, so another brainstorm can apply it
Exporting the session's theme: a CSS file of the overrides and a DTCG tokens file, with the path and Show in folder
After Promote: the WeekStrip row says a thread on robnet's project is adding it to the library, with Open thread, and offers no second Promote while it runs

The first message of the T3 thread Promote started on the library's project: which component, from which brainstorm, the library's folder and entry, its proposed files, and the example props for its story
Once the library is synced with WeekStrip, the open brainstorm offers version 2: Upgrade checks every block against it first
After Upgrade: the brainstorm builds with v2 and keeps its theme tweaks; the week strip now renders the library's own WeekStrip, untagged, and the Inspector lists WeekStrip under Now in the kit
The Versions tab: v1 and v2, each with when it was synced, what it holds, and the brainstorms that build with it
